water._doc: Water (render/shaders/water.gdshader). Ripples: the peak of the fetch-limited JONSWAP spectrum (Hasselmann et al. 1973, Dtsch. Hydrogr. Z. Suppl. A8 no. 12), f_p = 3.5 (g / U) (g X / U^2)^-0.33 with g = 9.80665 m/s2, the breeze U = 3 m/s (wind_speed_ms of the vegetation material) and X = fetch_m = 400 m, the width of a lake of the map (terrain_gen.cpp: a basin of radius 170 m, wobbling by 38 %, is 210 to 470 m across): peak_hz = 1.5399 Hz, wavelength g / (2 pi f_p^2) = 0.6582 m, wave_scale its inverse, 1.5193 cells a metre; the detail layer at twice the frequency, a quarter of the wavelength (detail_ratio 4), equal in slope by the f^-5 equilibrium range (Phillips 1958, J. Fluid Mech. 4(4)). slope_sigma 0.1355: rms of the Cox & Munk 1954 (J. Opt. Soc. Am. 44(11)) clean-surface mean square slope 0.003 + 0.00512 U = 0.01836. ripple_strength 0.1764: slope_sigma over the rms slope of the two noise layers as the shader sums them, 0.7680 (measured over 8 000 000 samples of lattice_noise.gdshaderinc). specular_f0 0.357: Godot's F0 = 0.16 SPECULAR^2 (F0() in servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl) for water's F0 ((1.333 - 1) / (1.333 + 1))^2 = 0.0204. shallow and deep: medians measured on the visual-target photo 14_lago_perto.jpg (registro/vegetacao-terreno/): shore box (60,195)-(620,215) where B > R + 10 and G > 110, 1343 pixels, (87, 131, 166); mid-lake box (40,230)-(300,300) where B > R + 20, 4375 pixels, (94, 120, 143). Those are screen colours; the albedos here are what shows as them in our render: the river of capture_landscape.tscn at noon, screen (186, 210, 219) from the mean of the albedos #5783a6 and #5e788f, gives the linear gain of the light on the water through the inverse of ACES (render/tone_map.gd), (2.27, 1.98, 1.57), and each target is divided by it.

terrain._doc: Terrain (render/shaders/terrain.gdshader). Slope bands as 1 - normal.y, that is 1 - cos(angle): dirt_from 0.117 = 28 deg and dirt_to 0.181 = 35 deg, loose soil shows between the low end of talus measured on Earth (28.0-33.4 deg, Kreczmer, Dabski & Zambrowska 2026, Miscellanea Geographica, doi:10.2478/mgrsd-2025-0032) and its repose angle near 35 deg (Francou & Mante 1990, Permafrost and Periglacial Processes 1(1), doi:10.1002/ppp.3430010107); rock_slope 0.234 = 40 deg, bare rock steeper than any loose debris rests.
